abstract: Hardness magnification makes lower bounds for the Minimum Circuit Size Problem (MCSP) at exponential thresholds a natural test case. Let $A_{n,S}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{N}$, $N=2^n$, be the set of truth tables computable by fan-in-two $\{\wedge,\vee,\neg\}$ circuits of size at most $S$. Fix $0<\mu<1$ and $S=\lfloor 2^{\mu n}\rfloor$. We show that for every permutation $\pi$ of the coordinates, the minimum middle-layer width $W$ of a strictly layered $\pi$-ordered branching program computing $A_{n,S}$ satisfies $\log_2 W=(1+o(1))S\log_2 S$. This holds simultaneously for deterministic, nondeterministic and parity OBDDs and for field-weighted ordered algebraic branching programs, and the same asymptotic holds for minimum width and total size after optimizing over orders. The upper bound is the prefix trie of $A_{n,S}$, bounded by a tree-pin enumeration of circuits. For the lower bound, a packed-selector family has matching entropy; a Fourier averaging argument chooses a linear quotient whose fibres meet both halves of any balanced cut, so the family is recoverable from either side; and an equality-graph argument extracts an identity submatrix of order $2^{S\log S-O(S\log\log S)}$ in the communication matrix at the middle cut, which bounds the width via rectangle covers or field rank. The witnesses depend on the order. The result concerns ordered models only: it gives no lower bound for free or general branching programs, one-tape machines or circuits, and no consequence for $P$ versus $NP$.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Proposition 2: the quantitative Lupanov bound is now referenced as Theorem 1.15 (Section 1.4) of Jukna [4], with the convention made explicit: fan-in-two circuits over {AND, OR, NOT}, size counting all gates including NOT gates, which matches the model of Section 1.
2. Section 6: the description of [2] is corrected and located in the STACS version: the N^{1.5-o(1)} MCSP lower bound for nondeterministic, co-nondeterministic and parity branching programs is [2, Theorem 5] and uses the Impagliazzo-Meka-Zuckerman pseudorandom generator, while Neciporuk's method is used in [2, Theorem 4] for MKTP; the read-once co-nondeterministic bound is cited as [2, Corollary 7] and the oblivious remark as [2, Section 1.2.1]. The comparison remains restricted to exponential bounds for ordered programs.
3. Section 6: added Volk, arXiv:2607.05944 [6] (almost-quadratic lower bound for an explicit function against read-once parity branching programs), distinguished from the present MCSP result.
4. Supplement: described as sampled balanced partitions with exhaustive enumeration of subspaces; the claim of an exact check of the averaged Fourier identity is removed; the redundant assertion ending in 'or True' is removed; README and script docstring updated; Problem and contribution section describes the check accordingly.
5. Main theorem: the (1+o(1)) statement is now preceded by the explicit bounds S log S - C_mu S loglog S <= log W <= S log S + C'_mu S, uniform in the order, the four models and the field; these bounds were already established by the proofs.
6. Section 1: circuit model made explicit (binary AND/OR, unary NOT counted, free constants) and total program size defined as the number of vertices.
7. Lemma 3: B_L is defined as a set of labels rather than a number.
8. Lemma 4: the proof now gives the explicit budget S_0 = S - 4n^2, the free-cell set T, the functions h_theta and the bound log|H| >= k2^q - |B_L|; the derivation of (9) from (8) via log|I| >= 2log|H| - log|A| - log 3 is written out.
9. Section 6: the unsupported sentence on sharpness of a one-tape transfer is removed; the paragraph now states only that one-tape lower bounds and class separations are not established.
10. No change to the truth of any theorem or to the abstract.
title: Tight Ordered Width for Exponential-Threshold MCSP
